problem.text: Six regular hexagons surround a regular hexagon of side length $1$ as shown. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?

steps.title: Where to start: the triangle is equilateral
steps.body: The picture looks the same after a turn of $120^\circ$ about the center of the middle hexagon, and that turn sends $A$ to $B$, $B$ to $C$ and $C$ to $A$. So $AB = BC = CA$ and $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral. For an equilateral triangle one length is enough, and the easiest one to read off the grid is the height from $A$ to side $BC$.

your_turn.prompt: A regular hexagon of side $1$ splits into six equilateral triangles from its center. How long is its longest diagonal (vertex to opposite vertex)?
your_turn.answer: $2$, because it is made of two sides of those small triangles, each of length $1$.

steps.title: Measure the height along the grid
steps.body: Side $BC$ is vertical and passes through the right vertex of the middle hexagon. Go straight right from $A$: first along the shared edge to the middle hexagon's left vertex (length $1$), then across the middle hexagon along its longest diagonal to its right vertex, which lies on $BC$. This horizontal path is perpendicular to $BC$, so it is the height of the triangle.

your_turn.prompt: How long is the height from $A$ to $BC$?
your_turn.answer: $1 + 2 = 3$: one hexagon side plus one longest diagonal.

steps.title: Get the side from the height
steps.body: The height of an equilateral triangle cuts it into two $30$-$60$-$90$ triangles. In each one the height is the longer leg and half of the base is the shorter leg, and the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times the shorter leg.

your_turn.prompt: With height $3$, how long is half of side $BC$, and how long is all of $BC$?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The area is half of base times height:
$$\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{3}\cdot 3 = 3\sqrt{3}.$$
The answer is **(B)**.
